Title: Media practitioners welcome return of 300-litre Budi95 monthly quota
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Malaysian Media Clubs (GKMM) has welcomed the government's decision to restore the basic quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres a month from Sept 1, describing it as a relief for media practitioners.
GKMM president Mohd Fauzi Ishak said the decision would particularly benefit media practitioners working in the states, who previously faced difficulties and had to bear higher monthly expenses for RON95.
"This expenditure is, of course, to cover the logistical costs of commuting to work, which also includes the need to travel to work and cover various programmes and events every day.
"The reinstatement of the Budi95 quota, as previously requested by GKMM, will certainly ensure that all media practitioners can continue to play their role in providing the best coverage, in addition to delivering information quickly to all citizens," he said in a statement today.
He said GKMM also hoped companies and media agencies nationwide would consider introducing new incentives or allowances for their media practitioners, in view of the rising costs involved in carrying out their duties.
He said travel and logistics costs were currently among the major expenses borne by many media practitioners every month, particularly those working in the states.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in his Prime Minister's Address for National Day 2026 at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) today, said the decision would allow more than 16 million consumers to continue enjoying subsidised RON95.
On March 26, the government announced that the Budi95 monthly quota would be reduced from 300 litres to 200 litres from April 1 following the conflict in West Asia, while the price of subsidised RON95 remained at RM1.99 a litre.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal tragedy: Missing trekker's son stays calm while awaiting news of father
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: As difficult as it is to wait for news about his father, who remains missing following the tragedy in Nepal, Mohd Firas Shabuddin has chosen to remain rational while praising the Malaysian government's continued efforts to handle the situation.
The 24-year-old engineer said he was satisfied with the comprehensive efforts by the ministries involved in managing the crisis.
His father, Shabuddin Mun, is among the Malaysians reported missing during a trekking expedition using a four-wheel-drive vehicle with the Team Loe group.
Although acknowledging that the situation had caused sadness and anxiety among the victims' families, he chose to remain calm and leave the rescue efforts to the professionals.
"We have to remain rational. If we allow our emotions to get the better of us, nothing will be resolved. Let the ministries do their jobs, as our task now is to pray and trust (in Allah)," he said when contacted.
On today's briefing session at Wisma Putra, Firas said it served as a good platform for coordinating information and ensuring all family members received accurate updates.
He said that during the closed-door briefing, the Foreign Ministry advised family members not to travel to Nepal for the time being due to limited access to the incident site, while informing them that the ministry would create a special WhatsApp group to provide daily updates.
He said families were also advised to refer to credible sources, such as Wisma Putra, Bernama and the official website of the Nepal Police, while family members were encouraged to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing at their respective state police contingent headquarters starting tomorrow.
"That is a very good move. Whether they are alive or not, at least the ministry is taking various actions to help us," said Firas, commenting on the recommendation for DNA testing.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Ashraf, 33, whose 63-year-old father, Mohd Padzil Darus, was also part of the Team Loe trekking expedition, said the group comprised nine Malaysians and one Nepalese national.
Ashraf said his family had agreed to undergo the DNA sampling process as a routine measure, given that the victims' whereabouts and condition remained unknown.
"Yes, this is a normal process and we all agreed to it because we do not know what happened. So, these are processes or steps that we need to take," he said.
He added that he last heard from his father about an hour before the tragedy occurred, when he received a photograph from his father showing the conditions and scenery at the expedition site.
Ashraf said his family was now waiting together for further updates while also holding special prayers for his father and the other group members to be found safe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Number of uncontactable Malaysians remains at 36 in China, 55 in Nepal - Foreign Ministry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The number of Malaysians reported uncontactable remains at 36 in China and 55 in Nepal, despite earlier reports that three Malaysians were among foreigners unaccounted for following a mudslide at Gyirong Port in Xizang, China.
In a statement today, the Foreign Ministry said it took note of reports by authorities in Xizang that three Malaysians were among foreign nationals unaccounted for following the mudslide at Gyirong Port on Aug 26.
"The ministry confirms that these three Malaysians are already included in the 36 Malaysians currently reported as uncontactable in China and do not represent additional cases.
"As such, the current figures remain at 36 Malaysians (in China) and 55 Malaysians (in Nepal).
"The Malaysian embassies in Beijing and Kathmandu are continuing to work with the relevant authorities to ascertain the safety and whereabouts of those who remain uncontactable, while cross-checking information from both countries to identify any duplication," the statement read.
The ministry said that over the past few days, the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu had also extended consular assistance to family members of Malaysians who remain uncontactable and had travelled to the Nepalese capital.
It added that the embassy had provided updates on the current situation and guidance on local procedures, assisted in coordinating with the relevant Nepalese authorities and, where necessary, accompanied family members to relevant facilities in Kathmandu.
"Family members were also advised to comply with all safety instructions issued by the Nepalese authorities, while the Malaysian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing continued to engage the respective authorities to gain access to areas closer to the affected sites.
"Any movement by Malaysian officers to these areas will be subject to approval by the relevant authorities, as well as prevailing safety and access conditions on the ground," it said.
Meanwhile, the ministry's Operations Room in Putrajaya continues to operate around the clock to coordinate information and assist Malaysians in the affected areas and their families.
Malaysians in the affected areas, as well as family members with relevant information, may contact the Foreign Ministry Operations Room at +603 8887 4570 or via email at dutyofficer@kln.gov.my.
The ministry also urged the public not to speculate or share unverified information while efforts to establish the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians concerned remain ongoing.
It added that further updates would be provided based on verified information received through official channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family returns from weddings to find home destroyed by fire
Article:
KOTA BARU: A family who had left their home in Kampung Pasir Kota for less than an hour to attend two wedding ceremonies returned to find their wooden house razed by fire today.
Neighbour Che Ibrahim Che Ahmad, 63, said the house belonged to a woman known as 'Mak Nik', in her 70s, who lived alone.
He said Mak Nik's daughter had come to the house after Asar prayers to pick her up for their friends' wedding ceremonies.
The former furniture worker said he was relaxing and about to take a short nap when he heard children screaming.
"I rushed out of my house and saw flames coming from Mak Nik's home.
"I immediately alerted my 59-year-old wife, Nor Azimah Ismail, as well as my children and grandchildren before we rushed out to safety," he said when met at the scene.
Che Ibrahim, a father of seven, said the fire spread quickly as the house was made of wood.
He added that Mak Nik's family returned later and were shocked to find their home destroyed by fire.
Meanwhile, his son-in-law, Ahmad Nukman Hanafi, 31, managed to save his Proton Myvi from being engulfed by the flames.
"Seeing the fire spreading, I immediately started my car and drove it to a safe place.
"I also managed to save two other family cars, a Perodua Viva and Toyota Alphard," he said.
A team of firemen from Darulnaim Fire and Rescue Station rushed to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 5.12pm.
They took about 30 minutes to prevent the flames from spreading to nearby houses and more than an hour to completely extinguish the fire.
The cause of the fire and total losses are still under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Some fatalities' in ferry capsize off Northern Cyprus
Article:
ISTANBUL: Some people died when a ferry capsized off Northern Cyprus on Sunday, the head of the local government said, without giving a precise toll.
"There are some fatalities," Unal Ustel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), said, according to Turkiye's state news agency Anadolu.
He added that 267 people had been on board the vessel when it capsized, and around 100 had been evacuated by rescuers.
The capsize occurred shortly after the ferry departed from the Northern Cyprus port of Kyrenia headed for the Turkish port of Tasucu.
Images broadcast by Turkish television showed the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its orange hull. The weather was sunny and several boats were seen in the area to lend assistance.
The TRNC, which is recognised only by Turkiye, controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.
Ankara occupied that part of the island that year in response to an Athens-engineered Greek Cypriot coup seeking union with Greece. The TRNC today is served with regular air and sea links to Turkiye.
"All necessary preparations are being made for a swift response from rescue and health services," the TRNC's health ministry said in a statement.
It added that hospitals in the territory had been alerted, so they could provide any medical attention that might be needed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak prepares for possible Disaster Emergency if haze reaches critical level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak is ready to declare a Disaster Emergency if the haze situation, which saw three areas record hazardous air quality readings, reaches a critical level, reports said.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk  Douglas Uggah Embas was quoted by the Borneo Post as saying that the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) was working closely with state and federal agencies to manage the haze situation in the state.
"Should the Air Pollutant Index exceed 500, the applicable guideline provides for the closure of government and private-sector offices and workplaces, except essential services, pending declaration of a Disaster Emergency by the National Committee on Disaster Management," said Uggah, who is also the SDMC chairman.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), three air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded hazardous API readings as of 8pm today.
Of the three, the Serian police station air quality monitoring station recorded the highest reading at 439, followed by Samarahan at 335 and Kuching at 319.
Two other areas in Sarawak, Sri Aman and Sarikei, recorded very unhealthy API readings of 278 and 222 respectively.
Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings ranging from 152 to 198. They were Limbang, ILP Miri, Kapit, Miri, Samalaju, Bintulu, Mukah and Sibu.
Taiping in Perak and Labuan were the only two areas outside Sarawak to record unhealthy readings, at 116 and 156 respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Peka urges public inquiry before Pahang forest reserves are degazetted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail has been urged to hold a public inquiry before permanent reserved forests are degazetted, with Pertubuhan Pelindung Khazanah Alam Malaysia (Peka) calling for greater scrutiny of such decisions.
Its president Rajesh Nagarajan said the organisation did not dispute the state government's jurisdiction over land and forests, but questioned why the public should be excluded from decisions that could permanently remove their protected status.
"If Pahang's process is truly transparent, responsible and 'working well', then hold a public inquiry," he said.
He also urged the state government to disclose the forests involved, affected areas, reasons for the degazettement, proposed developments and potential environmental impact.
"A public inquiry is not an attack on the state government's powers.
"It is a basic mechanism of transparency and accountability," he said in a statement today.
Peka also raised concerns over Sungai Pahang, citing reports of increasingly shallow stretches and exposed riverbeds in parts of Maran.
"Sungai Pahang is becoming increasingly shallow, with parts of its riverbed exposed in the Maran area, forcing the state government itself to study what should be done about the problem," said Nagarajan.
While stressing that Peka was not attributing the river's condition solely to forest degazettement, he called for scrutiny of the links between forest loss, land-use changes, erosion, sedimentation and river health.
"Environmental damage must be scrutinised and prevented before it happens, not addressed after the problem has become serious," he said.
Earlier, Bernama reported that Wan Rosdy said the state government's decision not to require a public inquiry before degazetting permanent reserved forests had been carefully considered.
He said land and forest management fell under the state's jurisdiction, adding that the existing process was functioning well.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smart team on standby, awaits Nepalese govt nod for SAR assistance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is on standby for deployment to Nepal to assist search and rescue (SAR) operations following devastating floods in the country.
The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) said the team's readiness followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's
directive and the government's decision to send it to Nepal.
However, the agency said the deployment would remain subject to the Nepalese government's requirements and official decision to accept Malaysia's assistance.
"Smart is currently on standby and ready to be deployed to Nepal.
"However, the team's movement remains subject to the needs and official decision of the Nepalese government to accept Malaysia's assistance," it said in a statement today.
Nadma said coordination on the matter was being carried out with the Foreign Ministry.
Meanwhile, Smart team commander Manaf Mat Isa, when met by reporters at Smart headquarters, said the team had made the necessary preparations for a possible deployment.
"Although tomorrow is the 69th National Day celebration, which will involve the Smart contingent taking part in the parade, we are ready, we have made preparations for a possible deployment to Nepal to assist in flood relief operations there," he said.
Checks by the New Straits Times at Smart headquarters today found personnel inspecting and checking search-and-rescue equipment as the team remained on standby for possible deployment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iceland votes 'No' to resuming EU talks
Article:
REYKJAVIK: Iceland voted 'No' to resuming membership negotiations with the European Union, final referendum results showed Sunday, dealing a heavy blow to Brussels which had been keen to welcome a new wealthy member.
In a vote held Saturday, 52.8 percent of Icelanders rejected the resumption of EU entry talks suspended 13 years ago, while 47.2 percent voted 'Yes', according to the official tally published by RUV, the public broadcaster.
The result will be a disappointment to Brussels, which had appeared willing to compromise on thorny issues to facilitate Iceland's accession.
The result will also likely bury the EU question in Iceland until at least 2028.
The country of just under 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of a 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy.
Membership talks were then suspended in 2013 when a eurosceptic government came to power.
Amid growing international tensions, Iceland's current government headed by Social Democratic Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir wanted to sound out Icelanders on deepening their ties to the EU.
The small North Atlantic island is already closely linked to the EU as a member of the European Economic Area and the free-movement Schengen zone – ties which will remain unchanged.
Technically, the referendum result is non-binding but the government has vowed to respect it.
The government will hold a press conference on Sunday at 1:00 pm (1300 GMT) to present its plans.
- 'We will be fine' -
Debates ahead of the vote had mainly revolved around domestic and economic issues, even if the war in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump's ambitions for neighbouring Greenland – which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions – featured in discussions.
The campaign had "lifted discussions about the EU, about Iceland's place in the world, about our general geopolitical situation and status, to a higher level", Frostadottir said on Saturday after she cast her ballot.
She was openly in favour of a 'Yes', but "we will be fine also if it's a 'No'," she said.
Frostadottir had vowed that if Iceland rejected the resumption of entry talks, the EU membership issue would not be put back on the political agenda during her mandate, which ends in 2028.
The government had also said that in the event of a 'No', it would leave to parliament the question of whether or not to formally withdraw the country's EU membership application.
Political analysts had said they did not expect the government to resign in the event of a 'No' victory. Made up of three parties with differing views on EU membership, it could emerge weakened by a rejection.
Had the 'Yes' camp emerged victorious, Iceland would have resumed its negotiations with Brussels, including on the hotly contested issue of fishing – a pillar of Iceland's economy and part of its national identity, and over which Reykjavik wants to retain exclusive control.
Any accession agreement would have then been put to a new referendum in Iceland.
The fisheries sector has been fiercely opposed to joining the bloc – 90 percent of companies in the industry are against the idea – and the EU had tried to woo them with a conciliatory approach ahead of the vote.
"Iceland's unique specificities on fisheries and agriculture are well known. They would have to be carefully considered," EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos had said.
"I'm confident that, together with EU member states, we would find creative solutions."
An EU source in Brussels told AFP: "I don't think anyone (in the EU) wants to block an accession over a question of fish."
Brussels had hoped to be able to present Icelandic membership as an example of positive enlargement that could also make it more palatable for member states to agree to take in poorer countries like Montenegro.
It would also have enabled it to enlarge its presence in the strategic Arctic region, and perhaps helped change some minds in ultra-wealthy non-EU member Norway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: Family pleads with govt to bring missing Malaysians home, whatever their condition
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: After nearly five days of anxious waiting, the family of 65-year-old N. Kalaiselvi, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, is urging the government to bring the missing Malaysians home, regardless of their condition.
Her daughter, Kritikaa Joyce De Brito, said the family appreciated the Malaysian government's efforts to coordinate the search and rescue mission, but acknowledged that their hopes were fading after nearly five days without contact.
She said that even if rescue teams successfully reached the affected area, the chances of finding the missing Malaysians alive could be slim given the conditions there.
"Even if they are found, they might be stranded in the forest or buried under eight feet of mud. The chances of survival are very slim.
"As such, our request is to bring them home. Regardless of the circumstances, whether they are still alive or not, we want them returned to us in Malaysia," she said after attending a closed-door briefing for next of kin at Wisma Putra here today.
Kalaiselvi was among 27 Malaysians who travelled to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, to perform religious ceremonies as part of a group organised by a local travel agency before losing contact following flash floods and landslides in Rasuwa District last Wednesday.
Kritikaa said all family members present at today's briefing agreed that the ministry should channel official updates and verified information directly to the next of kin.
She said the move was intended to curb speculation and the spread of false information that could further distress the victims' families.
"For now, the ministry is being very careful with what is released to the public. We understand this because we want to avoid any speculation," she said.
Earlier, Wisma Putra confirmed that 72 Malaysians in Darchen, China, were safe and receiving consular assistance, while another 55 remained uncontactable at the Nepal border.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 69 years on: What does Merdeka mean to Malaysians? [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Unity, freedom of choice and preserving the peace built by earlier generations were among the views shared by Malaysians from two generations ahead of the country's 69th National Day.
The New Straits Times brought together five Malaysians from the Merdeka and Gen Z generations to share their views on freedom, their experiences of Malaysia and their hopes for the country.
They were Lt Col (Rtd) Datuk Zarazilah Mohamed Ali, 86; former Special Branch officer Datuk Paul Kiong, 82; Petaling Jaya councillor Loh Y Lun, 26; researcher Graciely Stefanie O'Hara, 26; and gap-year student Rajdev Sachdev Singh, 20.
O'Hara said the freedom she valued most was the freedom of choice.
"I think a lot of decisions in my life I would not have made, or not been able to make, if I didn't have the privilege of choice.
"And I don't think that's a freedom that you appreciate until you're a lot older," she said.
Kiong, who spent six years undercover infiltrating the Communist Party of Malaya (CPM), said he wanted younger Malaysians to remember the sacrifices made in the pursuit of peace.
"I want them to remember that peace and harmony did not come cheap. It doesn't come free. It came with sweat and blood.
"We as senior veterans hope that they will continue to preserve the peace and harmony, to be united in our country as one nation," he said.
[[nid:1522234]]
Zarazilah, who witnessed the proclamation of independence at Stadium Merdeka as a 17-year-old Federation Military College (now Royal Military College) cadet, recalled the desire among young men of his generation to serve the country.
"When the country was immersed in fighting the communists, every young man wanted to be in the forces because we felt that being in uniform and fighting against the enemy of the country was the greatest, most honourable thing you could do for the country," he said.
Loh, meanwhile, said Malaysians today should stop dividing themselves, pointing to the unity shown by earlier generations in their pursuit of independence.
"If our forefathers could unite for one common cause to have a country we can all call home and help prosper together, we can put our differences aside," he said.
Rajdev said younger Malaysians should continue to recognise the contributions of earlier generations.
"I think we should appreciate what the generations before us did to give us a better future and a better Malaysia," Rajdev said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Over 1.1 million MSMEs to benefit from higher e-Invoice exemption threshold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 1.1 million micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will be exempted from implementing e-Invoicing following the government's decision to raise the implementation threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.
The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said that with the higher threshold, MSMEs with annual income or sales of less than RM3 million would not be required to implement e-Invoicing.
"This Madani government initiative reflects the government's concern in easing the compliance burden and costs incurred by MSMEs.
"In addition, the initiative gives businesses more room to focus on business continuity and expansion," it said in a statement today.
It said that since e-Invoice implementation began on Aug 1, 2024, a total of 265,379 taxpayers had submitted more than 1.84 billion e-Invoices.
However, the IRB said the government strongly encouraged MSMEs to participate voluntarily in e-Invoicing, in line with the country's aspiration to digitalise business operations.
"The IRB will continue to assist MSMEs through educational activities, guidance programmes and ongoing engagement sessions to ensure the smooth implementation of e-Invoicing.
"This includes guides and tutorials on using the MyInvois Portal, MyInvois application and MyInvois e-POS to raise awareness and understanding of e-Invoice implementation among MSMEs," it said.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in his National Day Eve address, announced
six measures
to ease cost-of-living pressures, support businesses and strengthen public services.
Apart from restoring the monthly
Budi Madani RON95
quota and increasing the Budi Diesel assistance quota, the other measures included raising the annual sales threshold for e-Invoice exemption from RM1 million to RM3 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia says preparing 'massive strikes' on Ukraine's energy sector
Article:
MOSCOW: Russia's defence ministry on Sunday said it was gearing up for large-scale attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in a tit-for-tat response to strikes by Kyiv.
"Russian forces have begun preparations for massive strikes against facilities in Ukraine's energy sector in response to the ongoing attacks by the Kyiv regime on civilian infrastructure and on Russia's oil and energy complex," it said on Telegram.
Last winter, Moscow repeatedly hit Ukrainian power plants, devastating the country's energy sector and plunging millions of people into cold and darkness in sub-zero temperatures.
Both sides have for several months escalated long-range strikes, targeting infrastructure such as warehouses, businesses, oil and port facilities, as well as ships, increasing civilian casualties.
On Sunday, the Russian army claimed to have struck a plant in Kyiv producing asbestos and cement whose warehouses, it said, were used to store explosives, as well as a manufacturer of drones and munitions.
On Saturday, a Russian strike on an ammunition depot in the suburbs of the Ukrainian capital triggered a huge explosion and killed at least 37 people.
Ukraine for its part attacked an oil refinery with drones in northwestern Russia, causing a fire, according to the local authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Survivors recount how Nepal landslides, floods swept away once-bustling bazaar
Article:
NUWAKOT (Nepal): For Santosh Thapa, his family was lucky when a devastating mudslide hit Devighat in Nuwakot, central Nepal, as all his relatives managed to escape the disaster, leaving their belongings behind as mud gushed into the area.
It was a narrow escape, Thapa said. Although he was in Kathmandu at the time, his relatives who were affected by the disaster told him what had happened, Xinhua reported.
"They first heard a terrifyingly loud noise, and then saw floodwater mixed with mud rushing towards them. Realising the danger, they panicked and immediately fled on a motorcycle.
"They probably had only one or two minutes to escape. If they had had to go on foot, they might not have made it in time.
"They took almost nothing with them when they fled," the young man told Xinhua on Saturday while helping his uncle and aunt clear the mud and debris from their house.
Thapa said his grandfather ran a shop on the ground floor of the house, but it was now completely buried in mud. The first and second floors were also affected by the mudslide, indicating that the mud had risen to about nine metres when it struck the area.
The house, shop, merchandise and household items were largely destroyed, with most of what the family had accumulated over the years lost, he said.
Thapa said there were about 300 households in the area, but only the elderly remained in the village, while their children lived in Kathmandu.
As a result, the actual number of people in the village at the time of the mudslide could not be accurately estimated, while the number of casualties and missing persons had yet to be fully tallied.
He said that when he arrived at the scene, he saw the bodies of two victims with his own eyes. One of them appeared to be a friend from his sixth-grade class.
A few kilometres upstream along the Trishuli River from Devighat, the scene in the main town of Bidur was equally heartbreaking. The once-bustling street of Trishuli Bazar had almost disappeared beneath thick grey mud.
Bridges crossing the Trishuli River and connecting both sides of the town were washed away, leaving some villagers unable to return home.
Some survivors returning to check on their homes after the disaster walked across the mud-covered ground. With every step, their legs sank into the soft, knee-deep mud.
Their shoes were sucked deep into the mire, forcing some to give up and trudge barefoot through it.
Aravindra Gupta, who has lived in the area for 25 years and ran a vegetable shop in the bazaar, recalled the moment the mudslide struck.
"I was sitting outside my shop when the mudslide arrived," he said.
Pointing to a vacant area alongside the river, he said his shop had stood there before the mudslide swept everything away.
Gupta, who is now staying at a friend's house, came from India at the age of one.
"I have already spent 25 years of my life here. I was only one year old when I came here. So, why would I go to India? I will stay here, but what can I do? What am I supposed to do? That's what I'm thinking about now," the 26-year-old said, perplexed.
At a nearby military camp being used as a transfer station for disaster victims, helicopters shuttled between the disaster zone and the camp, transporting the wounded and stranded survivors.
Outside the camp, family members of those still unaccounted for waited anxiously for the military to release the names of each new batch of arrivals, hoping to hear a familiar name.
Many had been waiting there for three or four days but had still received no news.
A local reporter told Xinhua on Saturday that it was the fourth day since the flood occurred and that the situation had yet to return to normal.
Rescue operations were ongoing, but rescuers faced difficulties reaching the affected areas as roads and critical bridges had been swept away at multiple locations, severely disrupting rescue efforts.
Telecommunications networks had also completely broken down, while electricity had yet to be fully restored in the affected areas, he said.
He added that official casualty figures had yet to be confirmed, although unofficial reports indicated that the numbers could be higher.
As of 9am local time on Sunday, 734 bodies had been recovered from mudslide-hit areas, with 2,498 people still missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
In the affected valley areas, temperatures were high and the air was humid. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned of the risk of disease.
"As always, when we have a disaster of this scale and we have displacement, overcrowding, and we may have disruption of water, sanitation and health services, and that can increase the risk of infectious diseases," said a UN report, citing WHO spokesperson Tarik Jasarevic.
Thapa told Xinhua that although local people had been provided with food, temporary shelter and medicine, he was concerned that the hot weather posed a risk of infectious diseases in the disaster-hit areas.
Many dead animals from the mudslide had not yet been found or removed. If human remains and animal carcasses were not properly disposed of, bacteria could multiply quickly and cause infections, he said.
"Searching for the missing and clearing away the dead are important; it is also necessary to protect the survivors and promptly carry out sanitation, epidemic prevention, and environmental cleanup work," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Takiyuddin: PH-Bersatu cooperation talk signals political shift
Article:
KOTA BARU: The possibility of Pakatan Harapan (PH) working with Bersatu in the upcoming Melaka state election is another indication that the two parties are moving towards political cooperation, said Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
Takiyuddin, who is also Pas secretary-general, said PH's openness to working with Bersatu, after previously cooperating with Umno, raised questions about the nature of the political relationship between the parties.
"Whether they want to cooperate in Melaka is something we do not know. That has to be confirmed by them.
"But if PH itself has confirmed that it is prepared to work with Bersatu, it becomes increasingly clear what is happening," he said.
Takiyuddin said the development could be seen as an admission by PH that it was prepared to establish political cooperation with Bersatu.
"It is like the saying, the clearer the light, the clearer the picture.
"This is a confession, an admission from PH that they will cooperate with Bersatu.
"It is another piece of evidence that they are moving towards establishing political cooperation," he told reporters today.
Takiyuddin was commenting on Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari's remarks that
PH was open to working with Bersatu
in the Melaka election.
Amirudin, who is the coalition's election director, said PH had no problem considering cooperation with various parties, including Bersatu, as political alliances should be assessed based on circumstances and the need to ensure a stable government.
He added that PH was prepared to consider various possibilities in Melaka, including cooperation with Bersatu, while ensuring that cooperation within the coalition remained intact.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families, friends cling to hope for three Malaysian climbers missing in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The families and friends of three Malaysian climbers reported missing following a flash flood and landslide in the Nepal-Tibet border area last Wednesday are still hoping for good news about their safety.
The three climbers are Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, who were reported uncontactable while undertaking a climbing activity in the Langtang Valley.
In a post on Threads, a friend of the three climbers appealed to the public to continue praying for their safety.
According to a post by user emyliatahar, the group's last message was received at 10.42am (Malaysia time) on Aug 26, the day of the incident, with their last known location detected around the Bhote Koshi area.
"We have reported the disappearance of the three of them to the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal as well as Wisma Putra to enable follow-up action and rescue operations to be carried out," she said.
Muhaimin is from Gelugor, Penang, Zaki is from Kubang Semang, Bukit Mertajam, while Adib Haikal is from Kulim, Kedah.
In another post on Threads, user myanaimah appealed to the public to pray that her brother-in-law, Adib Haikal, and his two friends are safe.
Meanwhile, Wisma Putra held a special briefing with the next of kin and family members today to provide the latest updates on the case.
Family members have also been asked to prepare to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing to assist in the identification process, following the discovery of unidentified remains in the disaster area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Manhunt in Switzerland after fatal rave shooting
Article:
AARAU, Switzerland: Swiss police were on Sunday hunting gunmen who opened fire at a rave, killing one person and wounding five others, some of them seriously.
The shooting, which happened in the early hours in Aarau, near Zurich, and sent partygoers running for cover, is a rare event in the Alpine nation, despite its long tradition of gun ownership.
The last major shooting occurred in 2001, when 14 members of the parliament and local government of the canton of Zug, near Lucerne, were killed by a gunman who then took his own life.
According to local media, shots were fired before 3am (0100 GMT) near the Aarauer Rave, an annual techno party attended by some 3,500 people at the Aarau racetrack from Saturday afternoon to Sunday morning.
"A 22-year-old woman died of her injuries at the scene. Four men and one woman, aged between 24 and 27, were taken to hospital. They are suffering from injuries ranging from minor to serious," local police announced on X.
"Searches to find the perpetrators, who are currently unknown, are under way," it added.
"Any possible motives as well as the exact circumstances of the act remain to be clarified."
Contacted by AFP, police were unable to say how many suspects there were nor the type of firearms used in the shooting.
A large-scale police operation swung into action in the area and beyond "as a precaution", the authorities said.
An AFP journalist saw armed officers deployed at the scene, the railway station and on the highway up to 30 kilometres away.
With the German border just a few dozen kilometres away, the investigation is being carried out in cooperation with Freiburg police, the DPA agency reported.
'SEVERAL SHOTS'
Media reports said an army helicopter was deployed in the cantonal capital, Aargau, as well as numerous police officers, rescue workers and medical teams.
Swiss news agency ATS-Keystone reported that police were alerted about gunshots during the night while police spokesperson Vanessa Rumpold told the Blick newspaper that "several shots" were fired at a large group of people.
Witnesses told Blick that shots were fired at about 2.30am while the rave was still taking place. Initially, they were believed to be fireworks but one witness reported "shots fired in bursts."
Many people sheltered in a nearby gymnasium for safety.
Swiss DJ Tekibo, who performed at the rave, wrote on Instagram that he was physically unharmed but deeply affected by the tragedy, in which he said he had lost a friend.
"Techno and raves are supposed to be spaces of freedom and safety, never places where something like this happens," he said, calling the events "absolutely heartbreaking."
"I'm still trying to process what happened because I lost an important friend and I don't have the right words for it."
A local resident in Aarau posted a video on social media showing deserted streets and what sounded like several gunshots in the background.
The Aargau cantonal police urged people to stay away from the area and asked for video recordings or photos from the rave.
The scene around the shooting was cordoned off on Sunday.
All of the victims were Swiss residents, police said.
Army reservists in Switzerland are allowed to keep their weapons, but not ammunition, at home. As a result, weapons are widespread but with no federal register it is difficult to know exactly how many.
According to the Geneva-based research centre Small Arms Survey, civilians had more than 2.3 million firearms in 2017 – nearly three for every 10 inhabitants.
That made Switzerland the 16th country in the world in terms of weapons per capita. - AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Restored Budi95 quota to provide relief, but enforcement must continue, says consumer groups
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's decision to restore the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidised petrol quota will provide much relief to Malaysians, but consumer groups said strict enforcement must continue to prevent leakages and abuse.
The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) said such a move would particularly benefit consumers with higher fuel consumption, while the government must ensure subsidised fuel reached genuine Malaysian users.
Its chief executive officer Dr Saravanan Thambirajah said consumers with higher fuel consumption, particularly owners of diesel vehicles such as pickup trucks and jeeps, would benefit most from the increase.
He pushed back against the assumption that such vehicle owners were automatically high-income earners, noting that in many rural and semi-rural areas, these were
"working vehicles" used by farmers, small traders and contractors.
"For them, fuel is not simply a lifestyle expense. It can be part of the cost of earning an income," he said.
Saravanan was asked to comment on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement during his National Day Eve address that the
monthly Budi95 quota would be restored to 300 litres
, effective Sept 1.
Anwar said the move was expected to benefit more than 16 million RON95 users, with the subsidised price remaining at RM1.99 per litre.
Saravanan said the government must ensure the subsidy reached genuine Malaysian users, warning that a higher quota would raise the stakes for enforcement.
"The government must continue preventing leakage, abuse and diversion of subsidised fuel," he said.
He said a well-managed targeted subsidy system would allow genuine consumers to benefit without ballooning government expenditure.
"When consumers are asked to make adjustments during difficult periods, they also need to see that temporary measures are reviewed and changed when the situation improves," he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysia Consumers Movement (MCM) legal adviser Sukhdave Singh concurred with Saravanan, saying the restored quotas would come as a great relief to many Malaysians.
"We believe reducing the RON95 quota in the first place was the wrong decision.
"Likewise, restoring the diesel subsidy quota to 400 litres is a welcome and necessary adjustment," he said.
He said future subsidy policies should be calibrated more closely to the actual needs and consumption realities of the people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMA calls for clear timeline, accountability for RM1bil EMR investment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should set a clear implementation timeline, measurable milestones and accountability measures for the newly announced RM1 billion allocation for Electronic Medical Records (EMR) and connectivity across public healthcare facilities.
Malaysian Medical Association president Datuk Dr R. Thirunavukarasu, however, welcomed the allocation, describing it as an important boost towards modernising the public healthcare system and enabling better connected care.
"The Health Ministry is not starting from zero, as over the last three years, digital clinics have increased four-fold.
"Through the One Person, One Record initiative, at least 15 million Malaysians already have health information, including prescription records, available through MySejahtera.
"With RM1 billion committed, there should also be a clear implementation timeline, measurable milestones, transparency on how the funds are utilised and accountability for outcomes," he told the New Straits Times.
Dr Arasu was commenting on a slew of initiatives announced by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in his National Day eve address.
He said these achievements reflected the work already being undertaken by teams driving the Health Ministry's digital health transformation, despite existing resource constraints.
Dr Arasu said the new allocation should build on this capability and accelerate what was already being delivered.
He said the investment must also address the hardware, connectivity and supporting infrastructure needed for the system to work reliably.
"Cybersecurity, maintenance, future upgrades and adequate recurrent funding must be planned from the beginning.
"Change management will be critical. Doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers who use these systems every day must be engaged and properly trained.
"Technology should improve workflow and patient care, not create additional administrative burden," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SME groups approve of 3 govt initiatives announced by Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Small and medium enterprise groups have welcomed three government initiatives announced today, saying these would help ease pressures on SMEs, micro businesses and small traders.
SME Association of Malaysia president Dr Chin Chee Seong said the measures were timely as businesses continued to grapple with rising operating costs and a challenging business environment.
"I appreciate that the prime minister and the government have seriously considered some of the concerns and requests that we have been raising on behalf of the SME community," he told the New Straits Times.
He welcomed the decision to raise the annual sales threshold for e-Invoice exemption from RM1 million to RM3 million, as well as the RM200 million Geran Sejahtera Madani for equipment for small traders, including home-based mothers, hawkers and night market traders.
Chin said the initiatives would provide much-needed assistance to smaller businesses with limited financial and manpower resources.
"The grants and financial assistance for small traders are also very helpful.
"For a large corporation, the amount may appear small, but for a micro business or small trader struggling with cash flow and higher operating costs, such assistance can make a meaningful difference," he said.
SME Association chairman Datuk William Ng said the initiative would benefit up to 80,000 SMEs with annual revenues between RM1 million and RM3 million.
He said businesses in this category typically operated with lean workforces and single-digit profit margins, making compliance costs a significant burden.
"With this exemption from e-invoicing, smaller SMEs will be able to focus on their business rather than spending resources on e-invoicing compliance," he said.
Ng said the Geran Sejahtera Madani, while targeted at small traders, would benefit the wider SME ecosystem.
He said hawkers, night market vendors and home-based businesses were at the front line of consumer commerce and key customers for SME wholesalers, food manufacturers and packaging distributors.
"Providing direct cash relief to the grassroots economy sustains domestic trade volume and ensures healthier cash flow across the entire domestic supply chains," he said.
On the government's AI for the Rakyat initiative, which will provide AI training to 100,000 youths, Chin said AI adoption was increasingly important for Malaysian businesses to improve productivity and remain competitive.
However, he said the training should not be restricted to a particular youth age group.
"Business owners, SME entrepreneurs, managers and employees of all ages need to understand how AI can actually be applied in their businesses," he said.
Chin also called for the government to engage industry players and SME associations when designing the AI programmes.
"We are in direct contact with businesses and understand the practical applications they require.
"The focus should not merely be general awareness of AI but practical training that businesses can immediately use, such as AI for productivity, sales and marketing, customer service, accounting," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Young Malaysians can get 3 months' free ILMUchat Pro from Merdeka Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians aged 18 to 30 can claim three months of free access to ILMUchat Pro from Merdeka Day after completing national artificial intelligence (AI) training under the AI Untuk Rakyat initiative.
The programme, which targets 100,000 young Malaysians, is a collaboration between the Digital Ministry, YTL AI Labs and MyDigital Corporation, delivered through the Rakyat Digital platform.
Participants who complete the required modules will receive unlimited access to the Pro subscription, which normally costs RM50 a month.
Eligibility and secure access will be verified through the national digital identity system, MyDigital ID.
In his
National Day Prime Address
today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the measure was part of a broader package to ease cost-of-living pressures and boost digital literacy.
YTL AI Labs chief executive officer Foong Chee Mun said the company was proud to support the government's goal of making Malaysia a leading AI nation.
"We're proud to support the government in advancing Malaysia's ambition to be a leading AI nation, starting with giving young Malaysians access to ILMUchat Pro.
"We look forward to empowering this generation not just to use AI, but to become the builders and contributors who define Malaysia's AI future," he said in a statement.
Built to reflect local communication styles, ILMUchat can switch between Bahasa Malaysia, English, Chinese and Manglish.
Its higher usage limits are designed to assist young people with tasks such as school loan repayment queries, SME grant applications, job submissions and building app prototypes without coding.
YTL AI Labs said its "sovereign AI" models were designed to be "culturally aware, contextually intelligent, and fluent in Bahasa Melayu" while performing on par with global standards.
To redeem the offer, eligible users must log in to the Rakyat Digital portal at rakyatdigital.gov.my, complete the learning modules and select the ILMUchat Pro reward on their dashboard.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian records hazardous API of 436, followed by Samarahan and Kuching
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality in Sarawak continued to deteriorate, with three locations recording hazardous readings and two others entering the "very unhealthy" category as of 5.45pm today.
Of the 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide, none recorded good air quality, while 50 were in the moderate range and 18 recorded readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Serian police headquarters in Sarawak recorded the country's highest reading, with an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 436, placing it in the "hazardous" category.
Samarahan and Kuching recorded API readings of 337 and 321 respectively, also placing them in the hazardous category.
Two other locations in Sarawak recorded "very unhealthy" readings, with Sri Aman at 260 and Sarikei at 210.
Seven other locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings: Sibu (195), Mukah (185), Bintulu (181), Samalaju (175), Miri (162), Kapit (161) and ILP Miri (159).
Meanwhile, Labuan recorded an API reading of 153, while Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 142 and Limbang, Sarawak, 130.
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded an API reading of 110, while Taiping, Perak, recorded 106.
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded an API reading of 105.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI for Rakyat programme to equip 100,000 youths with AI tools
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Youths aged between 18 and 30 will be eligible for three months of free access to selected artificial intelligence (AI) tools after completing six modules under the new AI for Rakyat programme.
The Digital Ministry said the programme, which begins tomorrow, would be rolled out in phases through the newly launched Rakyat Digital portal and aims to reach 100,000 Malaysian youths by 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the programme as one of
six immediate measures
for the people during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
"The programme is offered free to eligible Malaysian citizens aged 18 to 30, subject to completion and passing of the prescribed modules.
"The six modules are AI Nation 2030: Madani Approach, Cybersafe for Rakyat, Generative AI, AI Safety, Agentic AI for All and Cloud for Rakyat.
"Participants who successfully complete all six modules will receive three months of free access to selected AI applications and software.
"As an initial offering, eligible participants will receive access to AI tools from local and international technology providers, including YTL AI Labs' IlmuChat, Alibaba's Wonderclip and MuleRun, and Google's Gemini Enterprise," the ministry said in a statement today.
It added that more AI software and tools from other technology companies would be added progressively to broaden the learning experience.
Meanwhile, Digital Ministry secretary-general Datuk Fabian Bigar said the programme aimed to ensure youths not only understood AI technology but also had access to tools that could support learning, creativity and productivity.
"We want to ensure that the benefits of AI can be felt more widely and inclusively, in line with the government's aspiration to build a society that is digitally literate and prepared for the future," he said.
The programme is part of the government's efforts to expand access to AI while building knowledge, skills and confidence among youths to use the technology responsibly.
Rakyat Digital is the national digital learning portal and an initiative of the Digital Ministry led by MyDigital Corporation.
The initiative also supports Malaysia's ambition to develop an inclusive AI nation by 2030 under the MD2030 agenda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mat Sabu urges more Bumiputera farmers to go big in commercial agriculture
Article:
SERDANG: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu wants more Bumiputera farmers to compete in large-scale agriculture, encouraged by the growing number of young people taking up farming full-time.
"We hope the younger generation will take up agriculture full-time," he said at the launch of new pomelo and sweet potato varieties at Maha  2026 here today.
Mohamad said Bumiputera farmers should compete with communities already established in commercial agriculture.
"We must also compete in this sector because Bumiputeras can do it.
"But it requires full-time commitment.
"I am now seeing more Bumiputeras venturing into agriculture full-time, and that is what impresses me," he said.
He cited one of the recipients at the launch, a former engineer who now operates a 200-acre sweet potato farm in Terengganu, as an example of young Bumiputeras turning to commercial farming.
Meanwhile, the minister launched two new pomelo clones, Melomax 1 and Melomax 2, and the V8 sweet potato variety developed by the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi).
According to Mardi, six recipients received planting materials to support the expansion of the new varieties.
A total of 300 pomelo saplings and 30,000 V8 sweet potato cuttings were distributed for cultivation in Selangor, Kelantan and Sabah.
Maha 2026 is being held at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) from Aug 28 to Sept 6.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Langkawi ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes at Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis, where silt deposits are affecting navigational safety.
Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increased the risk to passenger ferry operations but could also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays.
"Ferry services are the mainstay of transportation to Langkawi and play an important role in supporting the country's tourism sector.
"Based on previous operational records, passenger ferry services are capable of transporting up to 25,000 tourists a day during peak season," he said in a statement today.
He said if dredging works were not carried out immediately, the situation could affect the smooth operation of ferry services, especially during peak periods, including ahead of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) next year.
Norhafiz said comprehensive and periodic dredging works were needed to ensure the shipping routes remained safe, while allowing ferry operations to run smoothly and accommodate increased passenger numbers.
In a related development, he said 176 regular ferry trips and 66 additional trips were scheduled between Aug 27 and Sept 6 to accommodate the school holiday and National Day crowds.
He said about 90,000 passengers were expected to travel via the two main routes — Langkawi-Kuala Perlis-Langkawi and Langkawi-Kuala Kedah-Langkawi.
He added that 86,978 tickets had so far been sold through online sales, counters and reservations.
"Visitors are also advised to buy tickets in advance online via the Cuti-Cuti Langkawi application to avoid disappointment," he said.
Norhafiz said the company would ensure a high level of readiness for ferry operations throughout the school holiday season and National Day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Malaysia's economic strength shines amid geopolitical uncertainty
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's six per cent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the second quarter of this year marks a new chapter in the country's journey towards greater progress and prosperity.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was particularly encouraging as it came amid an uncertain geopolitical environment, especially the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
"Imagine this, no one expected such growth based on the projections. No one.
"Not the World Bank, not the International Monetary Fund (IMF). No one projected the strength of our economy.
"But in the second quarter of 2026, Malaysia's GDP grew by six per cent," he said during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
Present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar said the positive achievement was the result of efforts and leadership built up since independence and was not achieved overnight.
"Approved investments and total trade reached their highest levels in history since 1957 and 1963. Malaysia's competitiveness rose to 15th place this year. The ringgit emerged as Asia's best-performing currency in 2025.
"The government and my cabinet colleagues chose the difficult path, strengthening the country's fundamentals, improving governance and restoring fiscal discipline.
"Closing avenues for leakages, expediting approvals and building confidence in Malaysia," he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said Malaysia's ability to remain peaceful and united despite its racial, religious and cultural diversity continued to be one of the country's greatest strengths.
"We have one homeland, Malaysia. We have inherited the history of a nation, and we are responsible for ensuring a glorious future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Economic growth benefits must be shared fairly among Malaysians
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government must ensure that the benefits of Malaysia's economic growth are shared fairly among all segments of society, regardless of race, religion, region or background, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the Madani government faced the challenge of balancing the needs of different groups, including the M40 and B40, Malay and Bumiputera communities, minorities, Sabah and Sarawak, as well as youths, women, persons with disabilities and workers in various sectors.
"How do we ensure the T20 continue to have confidence to invest? How do we protect the M40 and B40?
"How do we address the problems faced by Malays and Bumiputera, particularly those who are still feeling marginalised in certain areas?
"And what about the aspirations of the Chinese, Indians, Orang Asli, Sabah and Sarawak?" he said in his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre here today.
Anwar also said the government must take into account the needs of young people, workers, women, farmers, fishermen, hawkers and gig workers.
He said these challenges reflected the government's responsibility to ensure that development and prosperity were enjoyed by the people as a whole.
The finance minister acknowledged that Malaysians continued to face pressure from the rising cost of living despite the country's economic progress.
He said the government had increased allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM15 billion this year, the highest in the programmes' history.
"Does this satisfy me? No. Does this reduce the hardship caused by the cost of living? Not yet. We acknowledge that continuous measures must be taken," he said.
Anwar said the government had also introduced measures benefiting the M40, including a two-percentage-point reduction in income tax rates from 2023, which he said had resulted in RM1 billion in foregone revenue.
He said the government had also increased early schooling assistance to RM150 per pupil, regardless of family background.
On electricity subsidies, Anwar said the targeted subsidy programme had benefited 85 per cent of users, with the government spending about RM4 billion.
He said the government had also continued to strengthen grassroots programmes such as Kampung Angkat Madani, Sekolah Angkat Madani and Sejati Madani.
Anwar stressed that the government did not consider its work complete, acknowledging that many Malaysians were still struggling with living costs while small and medium-sized businesses continued to face cost pressures.
He said concerns also remained over infrastructure and access to healthcare, with Malaysians in various parts of the country still facing difficulties and long waits at hospitals and clinics.
"Every citizen, Malay, Iban, Kadazan, Orang Asli, Chinese or Indian, is a Malaysian citizen who must be given due attention and protection," he said.
Anwar said the government's priority was to strengthen unity while ensuring that the country's economic progress translated into better opportunities and living conditions for all Malaysians.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asyraf Wajdi, Dr Akmal to attend Pas Muktamar, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki  and Kelantan Umno leaders, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs, have confirmed their attendance at the Pas muktamar.
Pas and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said invitations had also been extended to other Umno leaders, including the heads of the party's Youth and Wanita wings.
"The confirmed attendees are the Umno secretary-general and Umno leaders in Kelantan, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs.
"Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh will attend the Youth muktamar.
"I understand that the Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad has also been invited. I am not sure whether she will attend, but there will be a representative from Wanita Umno," he said when met after visiting the muktamar venue here today.
He said PN would also invite leaders from its component parties, including Parti Wawasan Rakyat, Gerakan and Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia (MIPP).
Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and foreign guests would also be invited to the muktamar, he said.
"Among them are Islamic movements from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Türkiye, Indonesia and Thailand, as well as several other countries," he said.
On reports that Umno had invited Pas to its upcoming general assembly, Takiyuddin said Pas had yet to receive an official invitation.
"We have been told about it, but we have not received the invitation yet.
"If we receive the invitation, I am confident that Pas will send a representative there.
"So far, there is no official invitation. Personally, I have not received one, and my office in Kuala Lumpur has also not informed me of receiving it.
"However, verbally, there have been reports through the media," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Communications Ministry to step up efforts to spread information on government assistance
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry will step up efforts to ensure Malaysians are better informed about government assistance, initiatives and achievements.
Its minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry would help communicate the various measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including financial assistance and fuel subsidies, and ensure the information reached the public effectively.
"This is something we will help communicate to the public, so that the message from the Prime Minister on the government's efforts, achievements and assistance provided reaches Malaysians," he told reporters here today after Anwar's National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.
Fahmi said the government had allocated RM15 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) this year, while RM40 billion had been set aside for RON95 and diesel subsidies under the Budi Madani programmes.
"The figures for the assistance provided by the government are actually very large," he said.
He said the STR allocation was significantly higher than the amount previously provided under earlier assistance schemes, including Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia.
Earlier, Anwar announced that the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) subsidised petrol quota would be restored to 300 litres, while the monthly diesel allocation for eligible four-wheel-drive and pickup owners would be increased to 400 litres, effective Sept 1.
Fahmi said his ministry would also communicate other measures announced during the address, including the decision to raise the e-Invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.
The move is expected to benefit more than 1.1 million businesses.
The government also increased the allocation for digital healthcare initiatives from RM650 million to RM1 billion to accelerate digital access, including public Wi-Fi at government clinics and hospitals and the expansion of electronic medical records.
Meanwhile, 100,000 Malaysians aged between 18 and 30 will have the opportunity to receive three months' free subscriptions to three AI applications after completing the AI Untuk Rakyat programme.
Fahmi said further details on the AI initiative would be provided by the Digital Ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighter's brother to join Smart mission in Nepal to search for missing sibling
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The brother of Malaysian firefighter Mohd Fakhrul Munir, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, will join the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) mission to the country following the disaster in Rasuwa.
Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said he would join the rescue mission as a member of the team while also hoping to obtain news on the whereabouts and condition of his 44-year-old younger brother, known as 'Loe'.
He said he would make full use of the opportunity to enter Nepal to contribute his expertise to the rescue efforts while continuing to seek information on his brother.
"We will try our best, InsyaAllah. I also thank the government for providing us with this opportunity. I am a rescuer myself, but more importantly, I have a brother there," he told reporters after attending a meeting with Wisma Putra representatives here today.
Saiful said he hoped his presence in Nepal would enable him to contribute to the rescue mission while providing some relief to the family, which is still waiting for news of Mohd Fakhrul.
Yesterday, Saiful said he and his family remained positive and hoped Fakhrul and his friends were safe after losing contact with them following the disaster in Rasuwa.
He said the family still hoped the loss of contact was caused by communication disruptions following the disaster and that Fakhrul and his friends were safe.
Earlier today, family members of Malaysians who remain uncontactable following flash floods and landslides in Nepal began arriving at Wisma Putra here from 10am.
The meeting, held at 11am, allowed the families to receive briefings from the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Council on the status of their family members and search efforts in the disaster-hit areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
